table.name: badges
table.purpose: Stack-Overflow-style badge awards: one row per badge earned by a user, with the badge name and the date it was awarded. Part of a Q&A forum dump (posts, users, votes, comments, tags, etc.).

Date.name: awarded_at
Date.description: Timestamp when the badge was awarded to the user. Range 2010-07-19 to 2014-09-14; the spike on 2014-07-02 (899 awards) suggests a bulk/migration award event.

Id.name: badge_id
Id.description: Primary key; unique identifier for this badge-award row.

Name.name: badge_name
Name.description: Name of the badge awarded (e.g. Student, Supporter, Editor, Scholar, Teacher, Autobiographer). Some values look like topic tags (correlation, pca, modeling), suggesting participation-based badges named after tags.

UserId.name: user_id
UserId.description: Foreign key to users.Id; the user who earned the badge. Many-to-one: users can earn many badges.

table.name: comments
table.purpose: Comments posted on questions/answers in a Stack Exchange-style Q&A forum (likely Cross Validated, given statistics-related content). Each row is one comment made by a user on a post, with its score (upvotes) and timestamp. This is the standard Stack Exchange Comments table (cf. posts, votes, badges, postHistory, postLinks, users, tags).

CreationDate.name: CreationDate
CreationDate.description: Timestamp when the comment was created. Range 2009-02-02 to 2014-09-14, consistent with the site's activity period.

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key of the comment; unique integer identifier.

PostId.name: PostId
PostId.description: Foreign key to posts.Id — the question or answer the comment was posted on. Many comments per post.

Score.name: Score
Score.description: Upvote count of the comment (net score). Mostly 0 (77%), max 90.

Text.name: Text
Text.description: Body text of the comment. Contains @username replies, thanks, moderation notes — typical comment content.

UserDisplayName.name: UserDisplayName
UserDisplayName.description: Display name of the comment author, populated only when the author's user account no longer exists (98.4% null; values like 'user10525' are anonymized deleted accounts, others are real names). Complements UserId.

UserId.name: UserId
UserId.description: Foreign key to users.Id — the comment author. Null (1.6%) when the account was deleted, in which case UserDisplayName is populated instead.

table.name: postHistory
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style post revision history: one row per event/revision on a post (initial creation, edits, closure, reopen, tag changes, etc.).

Comment.name: Comment
Comment.description: Editor/system comment describing the change, e.g. 'edited body', 'added 1 characters in body', 'removed signature and greetings'; empty for most events.

CreationDate.name: CreationDate
CreationDate.description: Timestamp when the history event/revision occurred.

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key of the post history event.

PostHistoryTypeId.name: PostHistoryTypeId
PostHistoryTypeId.description: Code for the type of history event (Stack Exchange PostHistoryTypeId scheme: 1=initial title, 2=initial body, 3=initial tags, 4=edit title, 5=edit body, 6=edit tags, 10/11/12=closed/reopened/bounty, 33/35/36=hold/notice, etc.). No lookup table or join evidence is available, so the exact mapping beyond the common low values is inferred from Stack Exchange conventions; another reading (a site-specific or differently ordered code list) also fits.

PostId.name: PostId
PostId.description: Foreign key to posts.Id, the post this history event applies to.

RevisionGUID.name: RevisionGUID
RevisionGUID.description: UUID grouping the history rows that belong to the same revision of a post (multiple rows share a GUID when title/body/tags changed together).

Text.name: Text
Text.description: Content captured by the event: the post body/title text for edit events, tag names for tag events, or JSON (e.g. close voters) for moderation events.

UserDisplayName.name: UserDisplayName
UserDisplayName.description: Display name of the user who made the change, populated only when no UserId (e.g. deleted users); mostly empty.

UserId.name: UserId
UserId.description: Foreign key to users.Id, the user who performed the event; -1 denotes the system/community user; null for some events.

table.name: postLinks
table.purpose: Links between posts on a Stack Overflow-style Q&A site: each row records that one post (PostId) is related to another post (RelatedPostId), either as a plain related/linked post (LinkTypeId=1) or as a duplicate (LinkTypeId=3). This matches the standard Stack Exchange PostLinks export.

CreationDate.name: CreationDate
CreationDate.description: Timestamp when the link between the two posts was created.

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key of the post link row; unique integer identifier.

LinkTypeId.name: LinkTypeId
LinkTypeId.description: Type of link between the posts. Only two values occur: 1 (10186 rows) and 3 (916 rows). In the standard Stack Exchange schema these mean 1 = 'Linked' (related post) and 3 = 'Duplicate' (post marked as duplicate of another). The code meanings are inferred from the standard schema, not from a lookup table in this database, so an alternative reading of the numeric codes cannot be fully ruled out.

PostId.name: PostId
PostId.description: Id of the post from which the link originates; references posts.Id (many links can point from one post).

RelatedPostId.name: RelatedPostId
RelatedPostId.description: Id of the post being linked to (the related or duplicate target); references posts.Id.

table.name: posts
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style Q&A posts (questions, answers, tag wikis) from a statistics site (likely Cross Validated). Each row is one post; questions (PostTypeId=1) and answers (PostTypeId=2) share this table, with answers pointing to their question via ParentId.

AcceptedAnswerId.name: AcceptedAnswerId
AcceptedAnswerId.description: Id of the answer post accepted as the best answer by the question's asker; null for answers and unanswered questions. References posts.Id (self-join).

AnswerCount.name: AnswerCount
AnswerCount.description: Number of answers received by a question; null for non-question posts.

Body.name: Body
Body.description: HTML-rendered body text of the post (question or answer content).

ClosedDate.name: ClosedDate
ClosedDate.description: Timestamp when the question was closed (no longer accepting answers); null for open questions and non-question posts.

CommentCount.name: CommentCount
CommentCount.description: Number of comments on the post.

CommunityOwnedDate.name: CommunityOwnedDate
CommunityOwnedDate.description: Timestamp when the post became community wiki (ownership/reputation transferred to the community); null otherwise.

CreaionDate.name: CreationDate
CreaionDate.description: Timestamp when the post was created (typo in column name).

FavoriteCount.name: FavoriteCount
FavoriteCount.description: Number of users who favorited/starred the question; null for non-question posts.

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key of the post; referenced by comments, votes, postHistory, postLinks, and tags.

LasActivityDate.name: LastActivityDate
LasActivityDate.description: Timestamp of the most recent activity on the post (edits, answers, comments); typo in column name.

LastEditDate.name: LastEditDate
LastEditDate.description: Timestamp of the most recent edit; null if never edited.

LastEditorDisplayName.name: LastEditorDisplayName
LastEditorDisplayName.description: Display name of the last editor when the editor's user account is unavailable (e.g. deleted user, shown as 'userNNN'); mostly null. Alternative reading: it may simply duplicate the editor's display name at edit time, but the mostly-null pattern fits the fallback-name interpretation better.

LastEditorUserId.name: LastEditorUserId
LastEditorUserId.description: Id of the user who last edited the post; -1 denotes a system/community user; null if never edited. References users.Id.

OwnerDisplayName.name: OwnerDisplayName
OwnerDisplayName.description: Display name of the post owner when the owner's user account is unavailable (deleted/anonymous user); mostly null. Alternative reading: a cached copy of the owner's display name, but the mostly-null pattern fits the fallback-name interpretation better.

OwnerUserId.name: OwnerUserId
OwnerUserId.description: Id of the user who owns (created) the post; -1 denotes a system/community user. References users.Id.

ParentId.name: ParentId
ParentId.description: Id of the question post this post is an answer to; null for questions and other top-level posts. Self-reference to posts.Id.

PostTypeId.name: PostTypeId
PostTypeId.description: Type of post: 1=question, 2=answer. The tags table points its ExcerptPostId and WikiPostId at posts rows, supporting 4=tag wiki excerpt and 5=tag wiki. Values 6 and 7 (moderator nomination and wiki placeholder in the standard Stack Exchange schema) have low counts and remain unconfirmed by the joins, so the full mapping is still tentative.

Score.name: Score
Score.description: Net vote score of the post (upvotes minus downvotes; can be negative).

Tags.name: Tags
Tags.description: Angle-bracket-delimited tag labels attached to a question (e.g. <regression><r>); null for answers.

Title.name: Title
Title.description: Title of the question; null for answers.

ViewCount.name: ViewCount
ViewCount.description: Number of times the question's page has been viewed; null for answers.

table.name: tags
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style tag directory (appears to be a statistics site, e.g. Cross Validated): one row per tag, with its usage count and links to its excerpt and wiki posts in the posts table.

Count.name: post_count
Count.description: Number of posts using this tag (usage count). Minimum 1, max 7244, heavily right-skewed.

ExcerptPostId.name: excerpt_post_id
ExcerptPostId.description: Id of the post (posts.Id) containing the tag's short usage excerpt. Null for ~42% of tags that have no excerpt.

WikiPostId.name: wiki_post_id
WikiPostId.description: Id of the post (posts.Id) containing the tag's full wiki description. Null when no wiki exists; typically one less than ExcerptPostId.

table.name: users
table.purpose: Registered user accounts of a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site (one row per user). Referenced by posts, comments, badges, postHistory and votes-related tables. Data snapshot appears to span 2010-2014.

AboutMe.name: AboutMe
AboutMe.description: User-written 'about me' profile bio, stored as HTML. Often empty or placeholder ('please delete me', 'merge keep' suggest account deletions/merges).

AccountId.name: AccountId
AccountId.description: Likely the global Stack Exchange network account identifier, unique per row; -1 is the anonymous/system placeholder account. Alternative reading: a generic external account id linking to a network-level accounts table (not present in this dump). No join evidence available to confirm either reading.

Age.name: Age
Age.description: Self-reported age in years (13-94, median 30). Mostly null because most users don't provide it.

CreationDate.name: CreationDate
CreationDate.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

DisplayName.name: DisplayName
DisplayName.description: Public display name of the user; not unique (common first names repeat). Values like 'user34964' are auto-generated names for anonymous/deleted accounts.

DownVotes.name: DownVotes
DownVotes.description: Count of downvotes cast by this user (denormalized counter; most users have 0).

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key: site-local user id. Referenced by posts.OwnerUserId, posts.LastEditorUserId, comments.UserId, badges.UserId, postHistory.UserId. Id -1 is the community/anonymous placeholder.

LastAccessDate.name: LastAccessDate
LastAccessDate.description: Timestamp of the user's most recent site access/login.

Location.name: Location
Location.description: Self-reported free-text location (city/country), e.g. 'London, United Kingdom'.

ProfileImageUrl.name: ProfileImageUrl
ProfileImageUrl.description: URL of the user's avatar image (gravatar, googleusercontent, facebook graph). The most common value is the default identicon gravatar.

Reputation.name: Reputation
Reputation.description: User's reputation score on the site (Stack Exchange-style points earned via votes and accepted answers); min 1, max 87393.

UpVotes.name: UpVotes
UpVotes.description: Count of upvotes cast by this user (denormalized counter; most users have 0).

Views.name: Views
Views.description: Number of times the user's profile page has been viewed (denormalized counter).

WebsiteUrl.name: WebsiteUrl
WebsiteUrl.description: Personal website URL from the user's profile; placeholder values like 'http://none', 'http://N/A' are common.

table.name: votes
table.purpose: One row per vote cast on a post (StackExchange-style data dump): up/down votes, accepts, favorites, bounty events, and moderation actions, each tied to a post and a date, with the acting user recorded only for certain vote types (bounties, favorites).

BountyAmount.name: BountyAmount
BountyAmount.description: Reputation amount of the bounty attached to this vote, in whole points. Populated only for bounty-related votes (VoteTypeId 8 bounty start / 9 bounty close); null for all other vote types, hence the ~99.7% null rate. Values are typical bounty sizes (25, 50, 100, 150, 200; 0 appears for bounty-close votes where the amount was already awarded).

CreationDate.name: CreationDate
CreationDate.description: Date the vote was cast (day granularity, no time component). Range 2010-07-19 to 2011-05-01, consistent with the site's activity period.

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key; unique surrogate identifier for the vote row.

PostId.name: PostId
PostId.description: Foreign key to posts.Id: the post the vote was cast on. Many votes per post.

UserId.name: UserId
UserId.description: Id of the user who cast the vote (references users.Id, though the join was not auto-detected). Null for anonymous vote types (up/down/accept, VoteTypeId 1-3), which are the vast majority; populated for user-attributed votes such as favorites and bounty starts/closes. Alternative reading: it could record only the target/recipient user for bounty votes rather than the actor, but the favorite-vote population favors the actor interpretation.

VoteTypeId.name: VoteTypeId
VoteTypeId.description: Coded vote type (StackExchange vote types): 1 = accepted answer, 2 = upvote (dominant, ~85%), 3 = downvote, 5 = favorite, 8 = bounty start, 9 = bounty close, 10 = deletion, 12 = spam flag, 15 = moderation, 16 = edit approved. No lookup table or join is present, so the code-to-label mapping is inferred from the standard StackExchange schema rather than from data in this database; another mapping could fit the observed codes.
